text: In responding to Leibniz's Identity of Indiscernibles argument, Clarke (on Newton's behalf) implicitly appeals to haecceitism — the view that two worlds differing only in their absolute temporal location are numerically distinct even though qualitatively identical.
explanation: This is true. Clarke resists the Identity of Indiscernibles by holding that there are primitive facts about which particular moments events occupy — a 'thisness' not reducible to qualitative properties — so two qualitatively identical worlds can still differ in absolute temporal location. Leibniz, by contrast, rejects haecceitism and insists that all facts about a thing reduce to its intrinsic qualitative properties.
